body:
support_lee: FYI — multiple customer tickets calling out p95/p99 spikes for generation requests from eu-west1 starting ~08:05 UTC. They see 600-900ms extra on the TLS handshake path and higher tail latency overall. Tickets attached: https://redwood.support/t/3456 :exclamation:

sre_jordan: I see a small correlated bump in our p95 telemetry for eu-west-1 edge (ingress) around 08:04. Traces show TLS handshake timeouts and occasional extra RTTs. Raising in #eng-sre.

netops_ana: digging into network metrics now. Quick checks: no scheduled maintenance, but BGP flap counter on one peer in eu-west POP jumped at 08:03.

observability-bot: alert: eu-west1.edge.tls_handshake.p95 crossed 250ms -> 820ms at 2026-11-05T08:04:12Z. Trace sample ids: trace::a1b2c3, a1b2c4, a1b2c9.

alice_prodops: Customers report increased 502/504 but mostly latency, not complete failures. Can we reproduce?

dev_kim: quick repro:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","input":"hello"}'
```
From my laptop in eu-west, I see the TLS handshake takes ~700ms for that time window.

netops_ana: paste traceroute + dig from a host in the eu-west POP (copied):
```
$ traceroute api.redwood.example
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.4 ms
 2  203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45)  1.0 ms
 3  198.51.100.12 (198.51.100.12)  30.2 ms
 4  * * *
 5  198.51.100.250 (198.51.100.250)  120.7 ms
```
and DNS lookup:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example @127.0.0.1
203.0.113.120
203.0.113.121
```
Noticed that the route jumps across an unexpected AS at hop 3 -> hop 5 causing a 90ms delta.

sre_jordan: that aligns with the BGP peer flap. Which peering is that?

netops_ana: looks like transit-AS 64521 had intermittent withdraws. Peering logs show session reset with our eu-west-agg router at 08:03:58Z.

observability-bot: bgp-session-eu-west1->transit-64521: resets=3, last_reset=2026-11-05T08:03:58Z.

alice_prodops: Any immediate mitigations we can apply to reduce customer impact?

netops_ana: options: 1) rotate announced next-hops to prefer alternate transit (we have secondary transit via AS64522) 2) pin traffic via our private peering (if route present) 3) increase DNS priority to ips in different POP (but DNS TTLs are 30s; will propagate slightly slower).

sre_jordan: Can we shift a fraction of traffic off the eu-west POP to eu-central or to dedicated capacity as a temporary fallback? We have routing policy to steer based on p95 window.

deploy-bot: canary-route-shift started by @sre_jordan at 08:14 UTC: 5% -> eu-central, 5% -> dedicated-eu, monitor for 10m.

dev_kim: initial canary shows p95 drop to ~220ms on canary path, main eu-west still high. Good sign.

support_lee: customers on premium tier still need lower tail — can we escalate route priority?

netops_ana: I pushed a temporary BGP community to prefer AS64522 for eu-west1 prefixes at 08:18 UTC. That produced a routing convergence ~08:20 and handshake times dropped.

observability-bot: eu-west1.edge.tls_handshake.p95 returned to baseline (~120ms) at 08:21.

alice_prodops: Nice. Any root cause notes? We should capture repro steps and postmortem bullets.

netops_ana: root cause: upstream transit-AS 64521 experienced a partial control-plane instability leading to transient withdraws; that forced traffic to re-route via a higher-latency path (cross-zone hop). Critical contributing factor: our BGP local-preference + communities allowed quick preference switch to the flap-prone transit.

sre_jordan: action items (short):
- netops_ana: confirm stable state and remove temporary community after monitoring 1h (done: 08:52)
- infra: add automated failover to prefer secondary transit earlier on handshake SLO deviations (ticket created: INFRA-981)
- dev-kim: add health-check based route pin override to avoid hairpin routes during short transients
- observability: add synthetic TLS-handshake micro-checks from multiple eu POPs and surface per-peer BGP resets in console

dev_kim: adding quick repro steps to the ticket:
1) run dig +short api.redwood.example against local resolver in affected POP
2) traceroute to observed IPs and capture RTTs
3) curl plus -w '%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer}' to capture handshake vs first-byte

sre_jordan: sample command I used: 
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "handshake:%{time_connect} total:%{time_total}\n" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
```
That helps separate handshake vs downstream time.

alice_prodops: timeline note: ticket opened 08:07, triaged 08:09, canary shift 08:14, full mitigation via BGP community 08:20, baseline restored 08:21. We'll write a short incident note for customers.

support_lee: I'll update impacted customers with the timeline and mitigation.

observability-bot: post-incident checks: runbook reminder — ensure bgp flaps map to routing preferences in Console.

netops_ana: follow-ups: schedule call with transit-AS 64521 ops, tighten BGP dampening for that peering, and create playbook for fast-transit-repin via communities (NETOPS-402).

sre_jordan: thanks all. Leaving this thread open for 1h post-restoration to catch any regression. If anyone sees a re-bump, ping @sre_jordan and I'll re-open canary shift. :thumbsup:
